Performativ
Seed round — November 2023

[SYNTHETIC RECONSTRUCTION. Assembled from public sources for pipeline testing.
Not a genuine Performativ document and never submitted by the company.]

The operating system powering tomorrow's wealth management.

One platform for portfolio data, advisory workflows, governance and client
reporting — for European wealth managers still running cores designed between
the 1980s and the early 2000s.

Copenhagen, Denmark. Founded 2020.
Offices in Denmark and the United Kingdom. Live in five countries.
www.performativ.com

Raising EUR 5.5M seed.

The problem

European wealth managers run on infrastructure built before the cloud.

- 24,000+ financial services companies in Europe still depend on core systems
  designed between the 1980s and the early 2000s.
- Those systems need 100+ hours of manual work every month, plus dedicated
  support staff, to keep client data and reporting straight.
- Portfolio data lands from several custodians in several formats. Nobody owns
  reconciliation, so the advisor owns it — in a spreadsheet.
- Every new client is an onboarding project. Every quarterly report is a
  rebuild, not a refresh.
- Governance is assembled after the fact. The audit trail is an inbox.

Net effect: the advisor's day is data janitorial work, and the client sees a
PDF once a quarter.

Replacing the core is a multi-year programme nobody wants to sponsor. So the
spreadsheets stay.

Our solution

One operating system across front, middle and back office.

Unify — multi-custodian portfolio data into a single validated book of record.
  Automated reconciliation, not a month-end clean-up.

Structure — onboarding, reporting, rebalancing and fee handling as configured
  workflows, with role-based permissions and audit trails attached.

Automate — the manual work that today needs dedicated support staff.

Scale — add clients and mandates without adding headcount or another system.

Published outcomes after implementation:
- Onboarding 200% faster than the industry standard.
- Operational cost reduced by up to 70%.

We are not a reporting tool bolted onto the legacy core. We replace the core.

The platform

Live today:
- Multi-custodian portfolio management; consolidated book of record.
- Automated reconciliation and data validation.
- Performance and attribution analysis; advanced analytics and reporting.
- Advisor operating environment — the day-to-day workspace, not a dashboard.
- Client portal and mobile application.
- Onboarding, rebalancing and fee management workflows.
- Role-based permissions, governance controls, audit trails.
- 100% EU data residency.

Shape of the thing:
- Cloud-native multi-tenant SaaS. No on-premise edition, by design.
- One platform serves wealth managers, asset managers, multi-family offices,
  investment advisors and private banks.

Out of scope, deliberately: we are a software vendor. We do not custody client
assets, we do not distribute investment products, and we do not intend to hold
a banking or investment licence.

Market

TAM — EUR 34B.
Global software and services spend addressable by a wealth operating system.
Derived as 3 basis points of roughly EUR 113T of professionally managed wealth
worldwide.

SAM — EUR 2.1B.
Europe. The 24,000+ financial services firms running pre-cloud cores, at a
blended EUR 87k annual contract value.

SOM — EUR 640M of ARR within five years.
Europe first. Land with small and mid-sized wealth managers, expand into
private banks and larger institutions.

Why now:
- Legacy core vendors are end-of-lifing on-premise products. The replacement
  decision is being forced, not chosen.
- EU data residency and operational-resilience expectations rule out a
  US-hosted stack for a large slice of the buyer base.
- Advisor headcount is flat while mandates, asset classes and reporting
  obligations keep growing.

— Market sizing on this slide is illustrative reconstruction. The 24,000+ firm
  count is the company's own published figure; the rest is not.

Competition

Three groups. None of them is a wealth operating system.

Legacy core platforms — SimCorp, Objectway, Temenos.
Deep functionality, built for institutional asset managers and large banks.
Multi-year implementations, on-premise heritage, priced past a 20-advisor
wealth manager. We win on time-to-value and total cost of ownership.

Point solutions — reporting tools, rebalancers, client portals, bought one at
a time.
Each covers one slide of the problem and adds an integration to maintain. We
win because the manual work lives in the seams between them.

Spreadsheets and the custodian's own portal — still the default at the small
end.
We win because the advisor's own time is the budget line.

Why now, why us: a Goldman Sachs trading-platform engineer and a data lead
from Nordic asset-management advisory, building the same system. The legacy
vendors have the functionality and not the architecture. The new entrants have
the architecture and not the domain.

— Reconstructed as a seed-stage competition slide. See metadata.

Traction

Assets on platform:
- EUR 20B+ in client assets under management running on Performativ.
- Live in five countries.
- Offices in Copenhagen and the United Kingdom.

Outcomes reported after implementation:
- Onboarding 200% faster than the industry standard.
- Operational cost down by up to 70%.

Commercial shape (illustrative):
- Roughly 20 institutional clients, weighted to Nordic wealth managers and
  multi-family offices.
- Multi-year subscription contracts, annual prepayment.
- Land on portfolio management and consolidated reporting; expand into
  onboarding, rebalancing and the client portal.
- Net revenue retention above 100% on that expansion motion.

— Assets on platform, the country count and the two outcome figures are the
  company's published figures as of the November 2023 seed announcement. The
  commercial-shape block is illustrative.

Business model

Subscription software. One revenue line. No interchange, no assets on our
balance sheet, no implementation-services business hiding in the numbers.

- Priced per platform, banded by assets under administration and advisor
  seats, with modules on top.
- Illustrative entry band: EUR 60-120k annual contract value for a 10-30
  advisor wealth manager. Six figures and up for a private bank.
- Multi-year terms, annual prepayment. Implementation billed once.
- Gross margin target in the high seventies at scale. Hosting and custodian
  data ingestion are the variable cost.

Expansion, not upsell theatre:
- Land on portfolio management and consolidated reporting.
- Expand into onboarding, rebalancing, fee management, client portal.
- Expand again by advisor seat as the client grows.

Go to market:
- Direct enterprise sales into small and mid-sized European wealth managers.
- Custodian and financial-infrastructure partnerships as the second motion.

— Every price and margin figure on this slide is illustrative.

Team

Albert Geisler Fox — CEO, co-founder.
Economics at the University of Copenhagen and the London School of Economics.
Led a data science team at Kirstein A/S, the Nordic asset-management advisory
firm, and worked as a financial researcher at TV 2 Business. Forbes 30 Under
30, finance. He watched a legacy-system replacement from inside a Scandinavian
wealth management firm in 2020 and started here.

Peter Barry — CTO, co-founder.
Executive Director of Software Development at Goldman Sachs — pricing
services, UI frameworks, trader surveillance — then led Development
Operations through a global trading platform migration. Before that, software
developer at Barclays Global Investors on a trading and analytics platform.

Founded 2020. The pairing is the point: the domain problem is data and
workflow inside a wealth manager; the engineering problem is a multi-tenant
book of record that reconciles itself. Neither half ships without the other.

Investors before this round: UpFin, iGlobe Partners, and EIFO, the Danish
state's investment fund.

The ask

Raising EUR 5.5M seed, led by FinTech Collective, with participation from
existing investors UpFin, iGlobe Partners and EIFO.

Use of funds (illustrative):
- Engineering — the book-of-record core, custodian data connectors, the
  advisor workspace.
- Commercial — enterprise sales and implementation capacity in the Nordics,
  Benelux and the UK.
- Compliance and platform — EU data residency, operational resilience, and the
  security posture a private bank asks about before it signs anything.

What the round buys (illustrative milestones):
- Assets on platform from EUR 20B to EUR 50B.
- First private-bank client live in production.
- Custodian connector coverage across the Nordics and the UK.

No ownership, cap-table or option-pool figures appear in this reconstruction —
none are public.

www.performativ.com

— Round size, lead investor and participating investors are the company's
  published November 2023 figures. Use of funds and milestones are
  illustrative.

metadata.not_a_real_deck: Synthetic fixture reconstructed from public sources for pipeline testing. Not a genuine investor document and never submitted by the company.
metadata.as_of: Traction, round and investor figures are as of the company's 2023-11-09 seed announcement. Product and platform wording is drawn from the company's current public website, so the reconstruction is not internally date-consistent.
metadata.purpose: Covers the POPULATED branch of the Track B verification checklist: unlike tests/fixtures/sample_deck.json (fictional 'Thalvik', deliberately unfindable), this company is real and searchable, so a research run should populate company.website_url and at least one FounderSummary.linkedin_url with real URLs rather than None.
metadata.illustrative_note: Market sizing (page 5), the 'commercial shape' block on page 7, all pricing and margin figures (page 8) and the use-of-funds and milestones (page 10) are illustrative constructions by the fixture author. They are NOT figures Performativ has published, nor claims the company has made. No cap-table, ownership or revenue figures are asserted anywhere in this fixture. Characterisations of the two real founders are limited to public professional facts published on the company's own website. The 'out of scope' framing at the foot of page 4 is the fixture author's inference from the company being a software vendor, not a published company statement.

planted_weaknesses.weakness: TAM is purely top-down (3 basis points of global managed wealth) with no external validation, and the illustrative SOM (EUR 640M) is ~30% of the illustrative SAM (EUR 2.1B), outside the credible ~1-15% band.
planted_weaknesses.honest_derivation: The figures are the fixture author's illustrative construction, not the company's. The counter-evidence is publicly findable: the global wealth management software market was valued at USD 6.39B in 2025 with Europe at 29% of it (Fortune Business Insights), roughly an order of magnitude below the page-5 TAM.

planted_weaknesses.weakness: The competition slide names legacy cores (SimCorp, Objectway, Temenos), point solutions and spreadsheets, but omits Addepar and the European direct competitors of Performativ's own profile (FA Solutions, Croesus). Should trip missing_direct_competitor_flag.
planted_weaknesses.honest_derivation: Addepar and Performativ are listed under the same Consolidated Reporting / Data Aggregation / Portfolio Management categories by a third-party wealthtech directory (andsimple.co), so the omission is materially checkable. The omission itself is a construction of this fixture for testing purposes and is NOT an observation about any real Performativ deck.

planted_weaknesses.weakness: The '24,000+ financial services companies' and '100+ hours of manual work every month' problem figures carry no cited methodology.
planted_weaknesses.honest_derivation: Both are the company's own published framing in its seed announcement, and neither is attributed to a study there. Flagging attribution is fair; asserting the numbers are wrong would not be.
